anvil:aws:KinesisStream.description: An Anvil-managed Kinesis Data Stream. On-demand capacity by default (set provisioned for a fixed shard count), and server-side encryption with the AWS-managed KMS key (alias/aws/kinesis) is always on. Add Lambda consumers with consumers (each gets a dead letter queue and safe retry defaults); use grantRead/grantWrite for other compute.

consumers.description: Lambda functions that read the stream. Each consumer gets an event source mapping (starting from the oldest record, bisect-on-error, 3 retries), its own dead letter queue for records that still fail, sqs:SendMessage on that DLQ, and — with grantRead: true — the grantRead permissions. All consumers share the stream's read throughput (2 MB/s per shard). Each consumer's resources are named after its consumerName, so adding, removing or reordering consumers only touches the one that changed.

maxRecordSizeKib.description: Largest record the stream accepts, in KiB, 1024–10240. Default: 2048, so the stream can take Aurora DSQL CDC events (rows up to 2 MiB) without extra config.

provisioned.description: Switches the stream from on-demand to provisioned capacity with a fixed shard count. When omitted, the stream is on-demand and scales shards automatically with traffic — the right choice unless throughput is steady and predictable.

retentionHours.description: How long records stay readable, in hours, 24–8760 (365 days). Default: 24. Retention beyond 24 hours is billed separately.

arn.description: The ARN of the Kinesis stream.

dlqArns.description: Each consumer's consumerName mapped to the ARN of its dead letter queue.

dlqUrls.description: Each consumer's consumerName mapped to the URL of its dead letter queue.

name.description: The physical name of the Kinesis stream.

batchSize.description: Most records sent to the Lambda in one invocation, 1–10000. Default: 100.

consumerName.description: Identifies the consumer and names its resources (<stream>-<consumerName>-dlq, -esm, -policy). Usually the Lambda's name, e.g. "indexer". Letters, numbers and hyphens, starting with a letter, up to 32 characters, unique per stream. Renaming a consumer recreates its resources.

enabled.description: Pauses the consumer when false: the event source mapping stops polling but keeps its position, so it resumes where it left off. Records older than the stream's retention are lost while paused. Default: true.

filter.description: Limits which records invoke the Lambda. Applied by the event source mapping, not the stream: the stream still receives every record, but records that don't match are skipped (not invoked, not billed). When omitted, every record is delivered.

grantRead.description: Attaches the grantRead permissions on this stream to the consumer's execution role. Declared here, not with a separate grantRead call, because the event source mapping must wait for the grant. false skips it with a deploy warning: the role must then get read access another way, or the event source mapping fails to create.

lambda.description: Wire an Anvil Lambda function as the consumer.

reportBatchItemFailures.description: Lets the Lambda report which records in a batch failed so only those are retried. The handler must return { batchItemFailures: [{ itemIdentifier: <sequenceNumber> }] }. Default: false (a failure retries the whole batch, split in half each time).

startingPosition.description: Where the consumer starts reading when it's first created. Default: "TRIM_HORIZON". Changing it later recreates the event source mapping, which resets the consumer's position.

anvil:aws:KinesisConsumerFilterArgs.description: Limits which records invoke a consumer. tables and patterns can be combined; a record matching any of them is delivered. Together they can produce at most 5 filter patterns (Lambda's quota).

patterns.description: Raw Lambda event filter patterns (JSON), for records that aren't DSQL CDC events. Kinesis record data is matched under "data", e.g. {"data":{"type":["order.created"]}}. Each pattern takes one filter.

tables.description: Delivers only Aurora DSQL CDC events for these tables, matched against the event's source.table. Qualify with a schema to also match source.schema: "orders" matches orders in any schema, "app.orders" only app.orders. Unqualified tables share one pattern; each qualified table takes one.

enum.description: Every record still in the stream, so a consumer that builds state (search index, replica, read model) misses nothing from before it existed. Default.
Only records written after the consumer is created, for consumers that only care about what happens from now on (cache invalidation, notifications).

anvil:aws:KinesisLambdaConsumerArgs.description: Lambda consumer configuration. Pass fn.arn and fn.roleArn from an Anvil Lambda component.

arn.description: The ARN of the Lambda function to trigger. Use fn.arn from an Anvil Lambda component.

lambdaRoleArn.description: The ARN of the Lambda's execution role. Use fn.roleArn from an Anvil Lambda component. Required for Anvil to attach the grantRead and DLQ permissions.

arn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) specifying the Stream (same as `id`)

encryptionType.description: The encryption type to use. The only acceptable values are `NONE` or `KMS`. The default value is `NONE`.

enforceConsumerDeletion.description: A boolean that indicates all registered consumers should be deregistered from the stream so that the stream can be destroyed without error. The default value is `false`.

kmsKeyId.description: The GUID for the customer-managed KMS key to use for encryption. You can also use a Kinesis-owned master key by specifying the alias `alias/aws/kinesis`.

maxRecordSizeInKib.description: The maximum size for a single data record in KiB. The minimum value is 1024. The maximum value is 10240.

name.description: A name to identify the stream. This is unique to the AWS account and region the Stream is created in.

region.description: Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints). Defaults to the Region set in the provider configuration.

retentionPeriod.description: Length of time data records are accessible after they are added to the stream. The maximum value of a stream's retention period is 8760 hours. Minimum value is 24. Default is 24.

shardCount.description: The number of shards that the stream will use. If the `stream_mode` is `PROVISIONED`, this field is required. Amazon has guidelines for specifying the Stream size that should be referenced when creating a Kinesis stream. See [Amazon Kinesis Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/dev/amazon-kinesis-streams.html) for more.

shardLevelMetrics.description: A list of shard-level CloudWatch metrics which can be enabled for the stream. See [Monitoring with CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/monitoring-with-cloudwatch.html) for more. Note that the value ALL should not be used; instead you should provide an explicit list of metrics you wish to enable.

streamModeDetails.description: Indicates the [capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-size-a-stream.html) of the data stream. Detailed below.

tags.description: A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.

shardCount.description: Number of shards, at least 1. Required, so a provisioned stream's capacity is always stated. Each shard takes 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s in and serves 2 MB/s out.
